# Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Context / Problem

Status mapping is hardcoded: outbound reads built-in `local_to_jira_status` at CREATE/UPDATE;
inbound inverts built-in `jira_to_local_status`, preferring a `rebar-status:<local>` label
hardcoded to `blocked`/`cancelled`. A project needing a remap/collapse has no echo-safe path. Make
it config-driven on the S1 core: **map-or-drift** (never coerce); remap/collapse round-trips via
`rebar-status:`.

## Dependency (prerequisite ticket)

On the S1 mapping core **[rebar:bfe7-0900-c3d1-4141]** (merged): `mapping_config` provides
`load_mapping_config(root=None)` + `resolve_for_project(config, key, *, builtin) -> MappingLayer`
(merges `builtin ← default ← projects.<KEY>`; `.status_map` local→Jira, `SKIP`=drop, ABSENT=drift).
`local_to_jira_status` is the `builtin`, so no `[mapping]` ⇒ effective map = today's default.

## Approach — one FORWARD seam; inbound stays reverse-map-free

Only **outbound (forward)** becomes per-project; inbound needs no reverse map/project key (the
`rebar-status:` label makes every non-built-in status self-describing).

1. **`config.py` — forward resolution.** Add
   `effective_status_map(project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` = `load_mapping_config(root)` +
   `resolve_for_project(builtin=local_to_jira_status)`. The literal stays the parity-tested
   fallback; `mapping_config` imported LAZILY (config.py stays stdlib-only).

2. **Outbound consumers read the resolved map via the `OutboundMapper` Protocol.**
   `outbound_differ._effective_status_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)` resolves the ticket's
   project (`projects_store.resolve_project`) and calls
   `config.effective_status_map(project_key, root=repo_root)` — the `[mapping]` overlay is read
   from the STORE ROOT (not the CWD, mirroring fetcher/preflight), threaded via a new
   `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root` populated in `run_differs`. The effective `status_map` (optional;
   `None`→built-in) flows into both Protocol methods — `map_local_to_remote` (CREATE) and
   `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE, via `compute_update_fields`); `_backend.py` + the two wrappers
   gain the param. Shared map-or-drift lives in `outbound_mapper.resolve_outbound_status`, reached
   by the UPDATE mapper (Cloud+DC) and both CREATE builders. `acli.transition_issue` is NOT
   threaded (gets the already-mapped name).

3. **Drift = leave Jira as-is, never a per-mutation failure.** Decided ONLY in the mapper: with
   no entry for a local status it **omits the `status` field** (Jira unchanged) + a drift alert
   (deduped per-status per-process so it doesn't re-flood stderr each pass), replacing today's
   `.get(status,"To Do")` coerce. `preflight_status_mapping` runs AFTER the mapper
   (`reconcile.py:485`): a drift carries no `status`, but a config REMAP emits a config-only Jira
   NAME absent from the BUILT-IN keys∪values it tolerates → spurious warning. Widen it (and the
   fetcher, step 5) to built-in ∪ a **NEW S2** `mapping_config.declared_status_names` (from
   `reconcile.py:485` `repo_root`).

4. **Generalised `rebar-status:` round-trip (built-in-reverse stamp rule).** Outbound
   (`outbound_labels`): `target = forward.get(local)` (GUARDED `.get`, never a subscript). A
   DRIFTED local (no target) → **no label**. Else stamp `rebar-status:<local>` **iff
   `config.jira_to_local_status.get(target) != local`**. On the built-in map this selects
   {blocked, cancelled} (`deleted` is lossy but excluded upstream via `excluded_statuses`) —
   default stamping preserved. Under ANY config remap/collapse, every status whose Jira target
   isn't the built-in canonical name for `<local>` is labelled → inbound recovers it. Inbound:
   parse the `rebar-status:<local>` suffix, validating `<local>` against a vocabulary DERIVED from
   `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` values ∪ `deleted` (cannot drift from a parallel literal) via one shared
   helper; the plain `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get()` fallback stays correct since every non-built-in
   status is labelled. (Malformed `[mapping]` fails closed via S1's `MappingConfigError`.)

5. **Fetcher known-set widened.** `fetcher._known_jira_statuses` today reads only built-in
   `jira_to_local_status` keys → a config-only status trips a spurious "no reconciler mapping"
   warning. Widen to built-in ∪ `mapping_config.declared_status_names` (from `repo_root`).

## Scope (files)

- `config.py` — `effective_status_map` (forward, lazy `mapping_config`).
- `outbound_differ.py` — `_effective_status_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)`; `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root`; thread `status_map` into CREATE/UPDATE + label diff.
- `run_differs.py` — populate `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root` from the pass `repo_root`.- `outbound_field_diff.py` — `compute_update_fields` forwards `status_map`.
- `_backend.py` — `OutboundMapper` Protocol: OPTIONAL `status_map` (default None) on both map methods.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — wrappers forward `status_map`; DC `_map_local_to_dc_fields` uses it (DC CREATE) w/ drift-omit.
- `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py` — shared `resolve_outbound_status` (map-or-drift, deduped alert); `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE).
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` (Cloud CREATE), drift-omit.
- `outbound_labels.py` — built-in-reverse stamp rule keyed on `config.jira_to_local_status` (guarded).
- `inbound_fields.py` — generalised `rebar-status:<local>` recovery via a DERIVED vocab (shared helper).
- `inbound_translate.py` / `apply_inbound_events.py` / `inbound_differ.py` — shared helper (retire `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`); `_LOCAL_STATUS_VALUES` re-uses the derived vocab.
- `applier.py` — re-export shared helper in `__all__`.
- `mapping_config.py` — **add NEW** `declared_status_names(config)`: every Jira status NAME declared across config (`status_map` values ∪ `statuses`).
- `fetcher.py` — widen `_known_jira_statuses` to built-in ∪ config-declared names.
- `reconcile_helpers.py` — widen `preflight_status_mapping` set (optional `repo_root`).
- `reconcile.py` — thread `repo_root` into the `preflight_status_mapping` call.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

Tier **in-process unit** — pure over the resolved map; tests hit REAL entry points; alerts are
non-fatal stderr via `capsys`.


## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Effective forward map = `local_to_jira_status` ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>` via S1
  `resolve_for_project`; a non-default overlay changes the outbound target through the real mapper
  — `test_status_config_effect`.
- [x] An unmapped status **drifts**: the mutation omits `status` (Jira unchanged) + a non-fatal
  warning, never skipped nor a failure — `test_unmapped_status_drifts`; the drift alert is deduped
  per-status per-process — `test_drift_warning_deduped_within_pass`.
- [x] A config remap AND a collapsed pair (OTHER than blocked/cancelled) round-trip losslessly via
  `rebar-status:<local>` labels, recovered inbound without a reverse map —
  `test_status_remap_roundtrip`/`test_status_collapse_roundtrip`.
- [x] The `outbound_differ` seam resolves the per-project map and reads `[mapping]` from the
  `repo_root`, not the CWD — `test_effective_status_map_for_resolves_project`,
  `test_effective_status_map_for_honors_repo_root`.
- [x] A config-only/remapped Jira status is tolerated by BOTH the fetcher known-set AND the
  post-mapper `preflight_status_mapping` — `test_fetcher_known_includes_config`,
  `test_preflight_tolerates_config_remap`.
- [x] The duplicated `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` literal is retired for a shared helper
  (re-exported in `applier.__all__`) whose recovery vocab is DERIVED (not a divergent literal),
  covering every local status the stamp rule can emit — `test_status_label_helper_single_source`,
  `test_recovery_vocab_covers_every_local_status`.
- [x] `value_maps`↔`config` parity tests in `state/test_config.py` stay green.
